[[File:Tannenburg.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Inquisitor Tannenburg{{Fn|3}}]]
He is famous for ordering the [[Order of Our Martyred Lady]] to attack the [[Scriptorum]] of [[Saint Garrat]], having the [[Battle Sister]]s drag hundreds of [[Adeptus Terra]] scribes screaming to [[excruciation]] chambers and burning down the structure. The [[Adept]]s lodged formal complaints with the highest authorities on [[Terra]], but were silenced when Tannenburg produced three hundred jars, each containing the remains of an executed scribe, his previously hidden [[mutation]]s uncovered for all to see.{{Fn|1}}

He is also known for destroying all forty-five members of the [[Psyker Cult]], known as the [[Coven of the Red Moon]].{{Fn|2}}

{{NecronsPortal}}
'''Tarekh''', also known as '''Tarekh the Undying''', was a [[Necron Overlord]] of the [[Nihilakh Dynasty]]. 

== History ==
Though at one point he was a mighty Overlord who ruled over many of the Nihilakh's [[Tomb Worlds]], following the [[Starheart Wars]] against the [[Eldar]] his power base was shattered and he has since plotted his vengeance.  Now ruling over the [[Tomb World]] of [[Cardrim]], Tarekh largely ignored the puny [[human]] settlements on the world and set about reactivating a millennia-old superweapon in order to carry out the wishes of his [[Phaeron]] [[Krispekh]] in launching a new wave of expansion.  However when Cardrim came under assault from both [[Ork]] and [[White Scars]] forces, Tarekh was forced to act against the invaders.  In the resulting [[Battle of Cardrim]], Tarekh was nearly victorious.  However his personal [[Catacomb Command Barge]] was destroyed by a [[Space Marine]] [[Dreadnought]] in the final assault against the fleeing White Scars.  As he self-repaired, a volley of [[Melta Torpedo]]es from an orbiting [[Strike Cruiser]] vaporized the Overlord.{{Fn|1}}

'''Targutai Yesugei''' was the chief [[Stormseer]] of the [[White Scars]] during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|2}} [[Magnus the Red]] once called his abilities "mighty" and said that were Yesugei a member of the [[Thousand Sons]], he'd be part of the [[Primarch|Primarch's]] inner circle.{{Fn|1b}}

===History===
Born on [[Chogoris]], when as a youth the boy named '''Shinaz''' was in service to a petty Khan and was tutored by a local shaman (or ''zadyin arga'') called [[Uig]]. When he was 16 (12 in [[Terra]]n years), he was ordered by his Khan to undertake a spiritual journey up the Ulaav Mountains on his homeworld in a challenge dubbed the '''Test of Heaven'''. While on the mountain, he had a vision of both the four [[Chaos Gods]] and the [[Emperor]], and was overwhelmed by a desire to resist and flee from the former.{{Fn|5a}} However when he descended from the mountain, he found his own camp had been burnt by enemy soldiers. Chased through the plains of [[Altak]], Shinaz used his nascent psychic abilities to attempt to fight back his pursuers. However in the end he was knocked unconscious, and when he awoke he found himself in the tent of [[Jaghatai Khan]]. Jaghatai announced that his name was now '''Targutai Yesugei''', and he was an adoptive member of the [[Talskar]] Tribe. Becoming close not to just Jaghatai but also [[Hasik Noyan-Khan|Hasik]] and [[Qin Xa]], Yesugei fought under the Khagan in his quest to conquer Chogoris.{{Fn|5b}}

When the [[Emperor]] arrived on Chogoris, Yesugei was inducted into the [[White Scars]] Legion and became a [[Space Marine]]. Being appointed [[Chief Librarian|Chief Stormseer]], Yesugei was known for his very close relationship to the Khan, serving as his chief adviser and ''de facto'' number two within the [[Legion]]. During the [[Council of Nikea]], Targutai argued in favor of the responsible and limited use of [[Librarian]]s and [[Psyker]]s in [[Imperial]] use and said they would be a powerful weapon against the enemies of mankind.{{Fn|3}} At the beginning of the Heresy, Yesugei was based on Chogoris while the Great Khan was waging the [[Chondax Campaign]], but sensing something was amiss rushed to meet up with him.{{Fn|1a}}

Yesugei's ship, the ''[[Sickle Moon]]'', encountered a [[Sons of Horus]] vessel which turned out to have been captured from survivors of the [[Drop Site Massacre]]. Learning of the [[Horus Heresy]] from the [[Salamanders]] Captain [[Xa'ven]], Yesugei and his new teammates journeyed to warn Jaghatai Khan of [[Horus]]' treachery, battling [[Word Bearers]] along the way.{{Fn|1c}} Plagued by dreams of Jaghatai's death, Yesugei and his new comrades eventually made their way to [[Prospero]], where they found the White Scars fleet in the midst of an attempted coup and [[Death Guard]] vessels closing in on them. Yesugei directed his small fleet against the Death Guard, and was saved from destruction only thanks to Jaghatai Khan returning to quell the coup and rally the White Scars.{{Fn|1d}}

Four years later, Yesugei was one of the few White Scars who had not lost faith in victory or had become demoralized during the grueling attritional war against the traitors, and believed that a path back to [[Terra]] would be found. That path eventually materialized in the form of the [[Dark Glass]] station, which Yesugei boarded in an attempt to study. However as the [[Battle of Catallus]] raged, [[Veil]], an agent of the [[Navis Nobilite]] who had infiltrated the White Scars fleet, managed to cause the station's destruction with [[Vortex weapon|vortex charges]]. As the station died, Yesugei attached himself to its [[Golden Throne|command throne]] and painfully sacrificed himself to force open a portal into the [[Webway]]. As his body disintegrated, Yesugei sent his psychic goodbyes to his three closest companions: [[Jaghatai Khan]], [[Ilya  Ravallion]], and [[Revuel Arvida]].{{Fn|2}} The portal allowed the Scars to return to Terra, where they proved instrumental in defending against [[Battle of Terra|Horus' siege]].

===Trivia===
{{Trivia}}
[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yesugei Yesugei] was the name of father of Temüjin, better known as Genghis Khan, whom Jaghatai Khan is partly based on.

(Formerly) |Notes = }} '''Tarik Torgaddon''' was the [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] of the [[Luna Wolves]] [[2nd Company (Sons of Horus)|2nd Company]] and a member of the elite [[Mournival]], an informal council of four captains meant to advise the Legion's [[primarch]], [[Horus]].{{Fn|1a}} He was known as a joker but an extremely skilled warrior.{{Fn|1b}} ===Biography=== When [[Garviel Loken]] was elevated to the [[Mournival]] following the death of [[Hastur Sejanus]] Torgaddon befriended him, his light-hearted, jokerish nature tempering Loken's strict adherence to the rules. Torgaddon helped Loken settle into his new role as a Mournival member and advisor to [[Horus]]{{Fn|1b}} and was the one to introduce Loken to the [[Warrior Lodges]], showing him that they were simply a way for Astartes of differing ranks and companies to come together as equals, which somewhat allayed Loken's suspicion of them.{{Fn|1d}} When the 63rd Expedition responded to the distress call of [[Khitas Frome]] of the [[Blood Angels]]{{Fn|1c}} Torgaddon's company was chosen to descend to the surface of [[Murder]] and search for survivors. Once there he struck up a friendship with [[Emperor's Children]] Captain [[Saul Tarvitz]] but developed a dislike for the arrogant [[Lord Commander]] [[Eidolon]], a feeling that became mutual after Torgaddon pulled rank, berated him for letting his lust for glory cause needless death, and telling him that Horus himself believed that Eidolon was an idiot.{{Fn|1e}} After contact was made with the [[Interex]], Torgaddon continued to act as 2nd Company Captain and advisor to Horus.{{Fn|1f}} When Horus was mortally wounded on the moon of [[Davin]] and people were crying out against the grief-driven killing of humans by Astartes, it was proposed by the Warrior Lodges to rid the fleet of these dissenting voices. Tarik refused to take part in this and quit the lodges over it. When it became apparent that the Legion's apothecaries could not save the dying Horus, Mournival and lodge members [[Ezekyle Abaddon]] and [[Horus Aximand]] proposed entrusting Horus to the Davinite priests, and move which both Torgaddon and Loken opposed, and for good reason, as it was the Chaos-worshipping Davinites who allowed [[Erebus]] to enter Horus's mind and sway him to [[Chaos]]. With Chaos's evil influence spreading throughout the 63rd expedition Torgaddon and Loken vowed to oppose it. When he and Loken discovered the Kinebrach blade used to injure Horus, they realized Erebus's treachery. When Tarik encountered Erebus, he held a knife to his throat.{{Cite this}} During the [[Isstvan III]] incident, Torgaddon was one of the loyalists whom Horus deemed too loyal to the [[Emperor]] to rebel against him and hoped to purge through a fiendish [[virus bomb|virus bombardment]]. However, once the loyalists received word of the treachery from Saul Tarvitz of the Emperor's Children, Torgaddon was among those captains who led the resistance against the [[Traitor Legions]] during the Isstvan III ground war. {{Fn|2}} Towards the end of the grim battle, he and Garviel Loken received word that their former Mournival brothers [[Abaddon|Ezekyle Abaddon]] and [[Aximand|Horus Aximand]] would be landing on the planet's surface to oversee the final elimination of the loyalists. Hoping to kill their betrayers and slow Horus' plans, they planned an ambush at the landing site, but Tarik met his death at the hands of the reluctant but resolute Aximand, while Loken looked on in horror. Tarik died physically on [[Isstvan III]] but his gene seed was removed and taken to [[Calth]] by Word Bearer [[Erebus]]. Erebus sacrificed his gene seed, along with gene seed from the [[Salamanders]], [[Raven Guard]], [[Iron Hands]] and even some from the [[Traitor Legions]].{{Fn|3}} Later in an arcane ritual, Erebus used the body of Tarik as a catalyst to create the [[Daemon]] known as [[Tormageddon]]. A strange by-product of this ritual summoning was that some fragment of Torgaddon's spirit remained sentient and free, and was able to communicate with his old friend [[Garviel Loken]] on [[Luna]].{{Fn|4}} ===Sources=== {{Cite}} *1: [[Horus Rising (Novel)]]: **{{Endn|1a}}: Part One, Chapter Four **{{Endn|1b}}: Part One, Chapter One **{{Endn|1c}}: Part Two, Chapter One **{{Endn|1d}}: Part Two, Chapter Five **{{Endn|1e}}: Part Two, Chapter Six **{{Endn|1f}}: Part Three, Chapter One *{{Endn|2}}: [[Galaxy In Flames (Novel)]],{{Cite this}} *{{Endn|3}}: [[Know No Fear (Novel)]], ''Target//Acquisition'', Chapter 8, pg. 100 *{{Endn|4}}: [[Luna Mendax (Short Story)]] *{{Endn|5}}: [[The Horus Heresy: Legions]] Card ===Uncited=== {{Uncited}} *[[False Gods (Novel)]],{{Cite this}} *[[Garro: Legion of One (Audio Book)]], Track 3 {{DEFAULTSORT:Torgaddon, Tarik}} [[Category:Characters (Great Crusade)]] [[Category:Characters (Horus Heresy)]] [[Category:Characters (Sons of Horus)]] [[Category:Loyalists from Traitor Legions]]

Tarn Marvolus.wikitext:
{{ChaosPortal}}
'''Tarn Marvolus''' was an [[Imperial]] [[Recidivist]], who fled from the [[Calixis Sector]] and later ruled the [[Koronus Expanse]] world [[Footfall]], between 499 and 500.[[M41]].{{Fn|1c}}
==History==
After the death of its{{Fn|1b}} founder{{Fn|1a}} [[Parsimus Dewain]], [[Footfall]] immediately became submerged in a struggle for political and economic control{{Fn|1b}}. Marvolus took part in this and rose to become Footfall's [[Imperial Commander|Liege]], through a campaign of assassination and the use of [[Chaos|dark sorcery]]. With the world under his tyrannical control, Footfall entered an era known as the '''Reign of Blades'''. Any who questioned the word of the soft-spoken Marvolus, was later found sliced into quarters—one in each of the four most distant points of Footfall. Despite this, his rule lasted for over a year, due to Marvolous' brutal alliance of criminals, [[Rogue Psykers|witches]] and narco-tribesmen. In truth, though, his reign was owed mostly to the indifference of passing [[Rogue Trader]]s, who cared little as to who ruled Footfall, as long as it served their needs. Marvolous grew to become too bold and arrogant, however. This caused his reign to come to an end, after he demanded that the Rogue Trader [[Cassilus]] pay him personal tribute for docking at Footfall. Cassilus replied that she would '''"pay a tribute of the kind she only paid to the greatest kings of untamed worlds"'''. Afterwards, the four quarters of Marvolous' body were later found in the four farthest points of Footfall.{{Fn|1c}}

Tarrian.wikitext:
{{ImperiumPortal}}
'''Tarrian''' was a [[Commissar]] and leader of the [[VPHC]] during the [[Siege of Vervunhive]].{{Fn|1a}}


==Biography==
In the course of the Siege, a series of communications breakdowns led [[General]] [[Grizmund]], commander of the [[Narmenian Armoured]] [[Imperial Guard Regiment|regiments]] sent to assist in the defence of [[Vervunhive]], to disobey the deployment orders that he had been given in an attempt to get his armour to reinforce the [[Veyveyr Gate]].  The VPHC, however, intercepted Grizmund, arresting the General and his officers and sentencing them to a court-martial.{{Fn|1b}}{{Fn|1c}}

The decision to punish loyal Imperial soldiers for trying to do what they could to prevent the conquest of Vervunhive by [[Chaos|The Archenemy]] did not sit well with a number of the [[Astra Militarum|Guard's]] officers; most notably, [[Colonel-Commissar]] [[Ibram Gaunt|Gaunt]] of the [[Tanith First and Only]] tried to have the trial overturned, even against the wishes of the ranking Guard commander, General [[Noches Sturm|Sturm]], who had been hesitant to enforce sanctions on Vervunhive's leaders and the VPHC for the sake of diplomacy.{{Fn|1c}}{{Fn|1d}} By this point, however, the Siege's situation had become grim enough that even Sturm agreed to release Grizmund. Tarrian tried to have Grizmund and his men executed before Sturm could intervene, but was gunned down by [[Colonel]] [[Gilbear]] of the [[Royal Volpone]].{{Fn|1d}}{{Fn|1e}}

Tatraziel.wikitext:
{{DarkAngelsPortal}}
{{Spoiler|source=Luther: First of the Fallen (Novel)}}
'''Tatraziel''' was the [[Dark Angels]] [[Chapter]]'s [[Dark Angels Supreme Grand Master|Supreme Grand Master]] during the [[Age of Apostasy]].{{Fn|1a}}
==History==
He would be the first [[Dark Angels Supreme Grand Master|Supreme Grand Master]] to end the cycle of torture that had begun under [[Zapherael]]'s hands. Instead, Tatraziel treated Luther civilly and tried to gain information about the [[Fallen Angel]] [[Machius]], who was aiding the renegade [[Cardinal]] [[Bucharis]]. If he did so, Tatraziel told Luther that it would show [[Lion El'Jonson]], that the traitor wanted his [[Primarch]]'s forgiveness. Instead, Luther related a story of his youth, where as a squire he underwent a quest to join [[The Order]], which required that Luther kill a [[Great Beast]] of [[Caliban]]. It was not guaranteed that Luther would prevail, so by law he would need to give up any rights that he had and would say his final goodbyes to his family. As his journey began, Luther would travel with a fellow squire named [[Galass]], who insisted they hunt in her ancestral lands of '''Greyhome'''. The lands were cursed, though, after being overrun by Great Beasts, [[Daemon]]s and Caliban's forests. It was after an encounter with the ghosts of Galass' ancestors, that Luther's companion abandoned him to continue on his own. Luther would not give up, though, and would prevail in his hunt. He would then join The Order, but he never discovered what became of Galass. Afterwards, Tatraziel surmised that Luther's story meant that the Dark Angels must become solely focused on their hunt for the Fallen, by giving up their past. It was only after every single traitor was dealt with, that the Chapter would be able to move on to a different future. Luther protested that was not what he had meant, but Tatraziel left{{Fn|1a}} and never returned to visit Luther again. He was later succeeded by [[Amathiel]].{{Fn|1b}}

Taurid.wikitext:
{{AdeptusCustodesPortal}}
'''Taurid''' was a [[Sentinel Guard]] in the [[Legio Custodes]]' [[Hetaeron Companions]], who took part in the [[Horus Heresy]]'s [[Siege of Terra]].{{Fn|1a}}
==History==
A proven exemplar of the [[Legio Custodes|Custodes]]' excellence,{{Fn|2}} he was among the one hundred [[Hetaeron Companions]]{{Fn|1e}} that [[Caecaltus Dusk]] commanded as the [[Emperor]] led a [[Teleportation]] attack on [[Warmaster]] [[Horus]]' flagship, the [[Vengeful Spirit]]. But due to Horus' machinations, the strike force's teleportation separated them all and the Emperor and the Companions found themselves alone within one of the Spirit's hanger bays.{{Fn|1b}} Soon afterwards, though, the Warmaster is able to manipulate the Companions' minds and convinces them that the Emperor must die. With this overwhelming thought, the Companions attack the Emperor and He is forced to kill many of them, before He can gather enough of His [[psychic]] might to clear the Custodes' minds of Horus' influence.{{Fn|1c}} The Companions have been ravaged, however, and few are still alive to protect the Emperor, as He ventures further into the Vengeful Spirit.{{Fn|1d}}

Their respite is short lived though, as the [[Chaos Gods]] strike and cloud the [[Hetaeron Companions|Companions]]' minds to the environment around them. This allows the [[Daemons]] infesting the [[warp]]-tainted [[Vengeful Spirit]] to silently attack the [[Legio Custodes|Custodes]] and many are killed this way, before the [[Emperor]] notices what is happening. Once more He is forced to use his [[psychic]] powers to clear the Companions' minds, but at this point only Taurid, [[Caecaltus Dusk]], [[Xadophus]], [[Karedo]], [[Ravengast]], [[Nmembo]] and [[Zagrus]] still live.{{Fn|1e}} As they venture further into the Vengueful Spirit they begin to be attacked on all sides and the Emperor extends his psychic might into the surviving Companions. Though their minds are still their own, the Custodes' become an extension of the Emperor's will and their eight bodies are controlled by His mind, as He searches for [[Warmaster]] [[Horus]].{{Fn|2}}

Tay'ama.wikitext:
{{TauPortal}}
'''Tay'ama''' is a [[Tau]] [[Fireblade]] from the [[Tau Empire]] [[Sept World]] [[Vior'la]] and was among its forces that conquered the [[Imperial]] [[Hive World]] [[Khollorn VII]]. However when Vior'la began pacifying Khollorn VII's population, the Sept World's [[Fire Warriors]] were attacked by [[Genestealer Cult]]ists that emerged from beneath the Hive World's surface. Singing the praises of their [[Genestealer Patriarch|Patriarch]], the [[Reaverlord Crucius]], the Cultists quickly surrounded the surprised Fire Warriors and began butchering them. Unable to retreat, the Fire Warriors fell to disorder, but amidst the massacre Tay'ama was able to rally a number of survivors to him and then led them in a hunt for the Reaverlord's lair. Using the geothermal scans provided by recon drones, Tay'ama's warriors discovered the Reaverlord's lair and killed the Patriarch, with barrages of pulse fire. The Reaverlord's death caused the Genestealer Cultists' attacks, to lose all cohesion and Vior'la's forces were able to drive them back underground, where they were destroyed by magmatic pulse-bombs. However nearly all of Tay'ama's group of warriors died, while fighting the Reaverlord and it is not known if Tay'ama survived the attack.{{Fn|1}}

Te Kahurangi.wikitext:
{{SpaceMarinesPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is the current [[Chief Librarian]] of the [[Carcharodons]] [[Chapter]].{{Fn|1a}}

Known as the '''Pale Nomad''', Te Kahurangi is the oldest member of the Chapter and is said to have been descended from the Wandering Ancestors, those that went into space at the behest of [[the Forgotten One]].{{Fn|1a}}

==History==
Te Kahurangi was recruited from a [[Ocean World]] that was a recruitment world for a unnamed [[Space Marines|Adeptus Astartes]] Chapter, alongside his younger twin brother [[Chaplain]] [[Tangata Manu]].{{Fn|2b}} After Te was recruited by the Carcharodons, Tangata Manu was eager to follower in his older brothers footsteps and also was able to eventually join. This left the rest of their family defenseless, and they were eventually killed by the sea monsters of their native homeworld. Te blamed Tangata for their deaths.{{Fn|2b}} Tangata Manu was on a quest to recover a Chapter relic, the Dark Glass, for over 1455 years, making Te Kahurangi of a age older than that as well.{{Fn|2a}}

Te, alongside 3rd Company [[Captain]] [[Bail Sharr]], led a Red Tithe to the world of [[Zartak]] to seek the [[Psyker]] [[Mika Doren Skell]] before he could be captured by the [[Night Lords]] under [[Amon Cull]] and used as a sacrificial vessel for the [[Daemon]] [[Bar'ghul]].{{Fn|1b}} During the battle on Zartak, Te was captured by the Night Lords [[Sorcerer]] [[Shadraith]] and intended to be used as part of the summoning ritual.{{Fn|1c}} Before Te and Skell could be sacrificed, Amon uses the opportunity to betray and kill Shadraith, allowing Skell to escape and use Te's [[Force Staff]] to disrupt the [[Void Shield]]s of the Fortress. This allows the Carcharodons under Sharr to launch a teleportation assault, and in the subsequent battle Te uses his abilities to crush Amon Cull with debris.{{Fn|1d}} In the aftermath of the victory, Te accepts Skell as an [[Aspirant]] to the [[Chapter]].{{Fn|1e}}

Te once again accompanied Sharr, this time to [[ Atargatis Prime]] to treat with the [[Ashen Claws]].{{Fn|3a}} He and Sharr next helped purge [[Genestealer Cult]]s and [[Tyranid]]s on [[Piety V]] alongside [[Tyberos]], the ''[[Nicor]]'', and Ashen Claws.{{Fn|3b}}

(Former) **[[Emperor's Children]] *[[Black Legion]] **[[Ezekarion]] *[[Slaanesh]] |Notes = }} '''{{PAGENAME}}'''{{Fn|1}} (originally known as '''Telemachon Lyral'''){{Fn|2a}} was a swordmaster, one of the founders of the [[Black Legion]], and a primary lieutenant to [[Ezekyle Abaddon]].{{Fn|1}} ===Biography=== Lyras was the [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] of the [[Emperor's Children]] [[51st Company (Emperor's Children)|51st Company]] and was originally born on [[Terra]]. During the [[Horus Heresy]], he served in the [[Honour Guard]] of [[Eidolon]] and was present on [[Ullanor]] during the muster of traitors there by [[Horus]]' order.{{Fn|4}} After the [[Horus Heresy]] and falling to the temptations of [[Slaanesh]] Lyras became the second-in-command of a warband led by [[Kadalus Orlantir]] that consisted of the Emperor's Children's 16th, 40th, and 51st [[Company|Companies]]. Captaining the warship ''[[Threat of Rapture]]'', Lyras took part in an assault by Kadalus on the forces of [[Falkus Kibre]], [[Lheorvine Ukris]], and [[Iskandar Khayon]]. During the fight, Lyras was badly injured by Khayon and captured as the trio escaped Kadalus' forces.{{Fn|2a}} Afterwards aboard the Thousand Sons vessel ''[[Tlaloc (Ship)|Tlaloc]]'' Lyras was remade by Khayon.{{Fn|2b}} Ultimately, Telemachon defected to the side of Ezekyle Abaddon and aided them in the [[Battle of Harmony]]. Following the battle with a clone of [[Horus]], Lyras continued to serve as a lieutenant to Abaddon, becoming the [[Herald]] of the [[Warmaster]].{{Fn|2c}} He would be rewarded in his service with shards of the sword of [[Sanguinius]], which he reforged into a mask resembling his face before its mutilation. {{Fn|3a}} Following the formation of the Black Legion, Lyras became the Lord of the [[Shrieking Masquerade]], a warband of [[Chaos Raptor]]s. Lyras became more and more twisted and began to express a degree of disdain for Iskander Khayon. At the same time, his infatuation with Nefertari only grew.{{Fn|3b}} During the [[7th Black Crusade]] Lyras was a key Black Legion commander alongside Khayon and Abaddon himself and took part in nearly destroying the [[Blood Angels]] [[Chapter]] on the planet [[Mackan]].{{Fn|1}} ===Sources=== *{{Endn|1}}: [[Index Astartes: Death Company]], pg. 10 *2: [[Talon of Horus (Novel)]] **{{Endn|2a}}: Chapter 4 **{{Endn|2b}}: Chapter 9 **{{Endn|2c}}: Chapter 19 *3: [[Black Legion (Novel)]] **{{Endn|3a}}: Chapter 3 **{{Endn|3b}}: Chapter 4 *{{Endn|4}}: [[Slaves to Darkness (Novel)]] Chapter 18 {{DEFAULTSORT:Lyras, Telemachon}} [[Category:Characters (Black Crusades)]] [[Category:Characters (Black Legion)]] [[Category:Characters (Born: Terra)]] [[Category:Characters (Emperor's Children)]]

Telemach had only served in his legion for 10 years before he was grievously wounded and was interred in [[Contemptor Dreadnought]] armour. However, he bitterly resented his new status.{{Fn|2a}}

'''Tenebrus''' was a [[Black Legion]]-affiliated [[human]]{{Fn|2f}} [[sorcerer]] and member of the [[Hand of Abaddon]].{{Fn|1a}}

===History===
Tenebrus was heavily mutated, which led some - like [[Kor Phaeron]] - to speculate that he took too much from the [[Chaos Gods]] and gave too little.{{Fn|2a}}

Holding together the fragile alliance of [[Black Legion]], [[Word Bearers]], and [[Iron Warriors]] on [[Battle of Gathalamor|Gathalamor]], the scheming Tenebrus in truth sought only the Ring of [[Bucharis]] for its ritualistic power. Once the ring was recovered and the [[Chaos]] Bone Cannon it powered disabled, Tenebrus fled Gathalamor with his new acolyte [[Tharador Yheng]] and the ring in hand. He did not see the battle as particularly important, instead merely being the first step to slaying a god.{{Fn|2}}

Tenebrus later was seen initiating contact with the [[Word Bearers]] under [[Kor Phaeron]] himself. Kor Phaeron informed Tenebrus of [[Star Child|a child]] who if awoken could bring ruin to the servants of Chaos. Tenebrus vowed to find the child at all cost.{{Fn|2a}} To do this, he and Word Bearers allies under [[Xhokol Hruvak]] and [[Pridor Vrakon]] gather sacrifices from the [[Black Ships]] in order to summon [[Kairos Fateweaver]]. However one head of the [[Lord of Change]] proclaimed he was bestowing a gift to Tenebrus, while his other head stated it was a curse for his insolence. Tenebrus fell to the ground as Fateweaver vanished.{{Fn|2b}} He next consumed a potion of his newly cursed flesh in order to allow himself to enter the mind of a [[Cultist]] on the world of [[Srinagar]], coming to learn that the Star Child may be born within the [[system]].{{Fn|2c}} During the subsequent [[Battle of Srinagar]], Tenebrus and Yheng reached the interior of the Astropathic relay station where he accessed the minds of [[Astropaths]] before using his own [[Athame]] acquired from Kor Phaeron to leave.{{Fn|2d}} He then continued his hunt for the [[Athame|Shards of Erebus]] for his own ends.{{Fn|3}} Tenebrus is later seen with Yheng as the rest of the [[Hand of Abaddon]] meets in order to rebuild the [[Anathame]] from the gathered shards.{{Fn|4a}}

Tenebrus and Yheng are subsequently hunted aboard a [[Blackstone Fortress]] by the constructs of the Hand member [[Iron Magus]], who seeks the shards of the [[Athame]] for herself. However Tenebrus can not stop Yheng from collaborating with the Hand member [[Augury]], who sees his acolyte as chosen by the [[Gods of Chaos]] and destined for greatness.{{Fn|4b}} Yheng is eventually captured by the Iron Magus, but is able to kill him and escape. She meets with Tenebrus shortly after, who still vows to protect Yheng from the other Hand members. However as their argument escalates, it is then that the very Blackstone Fortress betrays Tenebrus, impaling him with iron spikes. Yheng betrays his master and leaves him to die.{{Fn|4d}} Later after the [[Battle of the Stygius Gilt]], a dying Tenebrus is still aboard the ruined Blackstone Fortress. He swears revenge against Yheng but is swarmed by a pack of [[Ur-Ghul]]s and torn apart.{{Fn|4d}}

Teus.wikitext:
{{ImperiumPortal}}
'''Teus''' was a [[human]] [[aspirant]] of a [[Chapter|Space Marine Chapter]].{{Fn|1c}}

Teus was born on [[Baal Secundus]], the son of [[Uigui]] the water seller.{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|1c}}  He attempted to become an aspirant of the [[Blood Angels]], journeying to [[Angel's Fall]] to undertake the challenges.  He initially showed promise, as he was genetically compatable with the Chapter's [[gene-seed]].  However, during the trials, he fell and sustained a brain injury.{{Fn|1c}}  He was rejected and sent home with brain damage; as a result, his father often abused him and referred to him as an "idiot".{{Fn|1a}}

Two years later{{Fn|1c}}, Teus and his father were amongst the civilians drafted by the Blood Angels to defend the chapter's [[fortress-monastery]] on [[Baal]] against the [[Devastation of Baal|invading]] [[tyranid]]s of [[Hive Fleet Leviathan]].{{Fn|1b}}  In the aftermath, as Uigui lay dying from contamination caused by a tyranid parasite organism, Teus was approached by a [[Sanguinary Priest]].  Due to the losses the Blood Angels and their [[Successor Chapters]] suffered, all genetically-compatable Baalite youths were being inducted into the Chapters of the Blood.  The Priest determined that Teus's brain injury was repairable and, as he was still suitable for implantation, he was recruited.{{Fn|1c}}

==Notes==
*It is not stated in [[The Devastation of Baal (Novel)|The Devastation of Baal]] which Chapter Teus was recruited into.

'''Thaddeus''' is an [[Assault Marine]] [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]] in the [[Blood Ravens]] [[4th Company (Blood Ravens)|4th Company]]{{Fn|2}}, having been promoted shortly before the [[Tyranid]] invasion of [[Subsector Aurelia]].

==Early Life==
Thaddeus grew up a native of the [[Hive World]] [[Meridian]], in Hab Spire Legis. He became the leader of an under city gang, and was involved in one of the world's many riots. During one of these disturbances, [[Davian Thule]] noticed the young boy holding off rioters. Inspired, the Captain put Thaddeus forward for the Blood Raven trials, the first Meridian native to be accepted in 700 years. 80 years later, battle-brother Thaddeus became a Sergeant before even earning his first service stud. He has since earned a reputation as a brash and idealistic brawler; and made his name battling [[Feral Orks]] on [[Calderis]] and [[Typhon Primaris]].{{Fn|1}}

==Wargear==
Thaddeus is armed with a MK X "Hells Teeth" [[Chainsword]] and an Astartes Mk III [[Bolt Pistol]] at the beginning of the Campaign. As the campaign advances, pending the players choices he can be made to wield various [[Power Weapons]]. Thaddeus can also be upgraded with Terminator Honors which allows him to wear [[Terminator Armour]] and he and his squad can be turned into a [[Terminator Assault Squad]] which come equipped with [[Thunder Hammer]]s and [[Storm Shield]]s.{{Fn|1}}

In [[Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War II - Chaos Rising]] he can wield a [[Lightning Claw]], or a pair of same in Terminator Armour.{{Fn|2}}

'''{{PAGENAME}}, the Battle-King and Lord of Hosts,''' was a prominent [[Death Guard]] [[Chaos Lord|Sorcerer Lord]], who commanded the massive [[Chaos Warband|Warband]] known as the [[Legion Host]] within the [[Eye of Terror]] during the [[Legion Wars]].{{Fn|1a}}

==Overview==
Daravek became the main rival for [[Abaddon]] and the growing [[Black Legion]], as each sought to become the new [[Warmaster]] of [[Chaos]] and succeed the [[Primarch]] [[Horus Lupercal]]. The two Chaos Lords clashed frequently and Abaddon sent the [[Ezekarion]] [[Iskandar Khayon]] to assassinate Daravek six times, but the [[Sorcerer]] always returned to his Lord in failure.{{Fn|1a}} Their conflict finally came to a head when Abaddon took the majority of his forces and tried to exit the Eye of Terror in order to obtain the [[Daemon]] sword [[Drach'nyen]].{{Fn|1b}} Once Daravek learned that only a fraction of the Black Legion's strength was left behind to guard their holdings, the Chaos Lord led his Warband to ravage the worlds controlled by Abaddon. Afterwards he pursued Abaddon's main fleet as Daravek also coveted Drach'nyen, which he believed would grant him the favour of the [[Chaos God]]s and allow him to become the premier leader of the forces of Chaos.{{Fn|1c}} Using means unknown to the Black Legion, Daravek found Abaddon's fleet near the edge of the Eye of Terror and launched an attack that destroyed several of their ships. Having already suffered severe losses after trying to force their way out of the Eye of Terror, Abaddon readily agreed when Daravek offered to meet with him on neutral grounds.{{Fn|1d}} The two soon met on the dead [[Craftworld]] [[Taial'shara]] and each brought with them several of their Warband's leaders. Before they began their negotiations though, Daravek suggested they hold a duel between two of their Warband leaders, which was customary when opposing Chaos Lords met with each other within the Eye of Terror. Abaddon once again agreed and selected Khayon, while Daravek selected the [[Iron Warriors]] Chaos Lord [[Ulrech Ansontyn]].{{Fn|1c}}

During the duel between their champions, Daravek gloated to Abaddon about how his Warband had invaded the Black Legion's worlds and slaughtered the forces they had left to defend them. This enraged Khayon and he defeated Ulrech in a frenzy of attacks. He did not kill the Iron Warrior though and instead offered Ulrech a place within the Black Legion, but when it looked like Ulrech would accept the offer Daravek decapitated him. This caused Khayon to attack the Chaos Lord, but to the shock of everyone Daravek used his [[psychic powers]] to completely dominate the Sorcerer and forced the Ezekarion to kneel before him. He then laughed and told a dismayed Khayon that he had defeated the Black Legion Sorcerer during the battle of [[Drol Kheir]] and then had bound Khayon's spirit to him before making the Sorcerer forget their encounter.{{Fn|1c}} Before further conflict could break out between the two groups though, the [[Warp Ghosts|Warp Ghost]] [[Ashur-Kai Qezremah|Saronos]] suddenly appeared and deescalated the situation. When both groups confronted him, Saronos offered them a deal: he could lead one of the Warbands out of the Eye of Terror, but would only do so to the Chaos Lord whose offerings met the Warp Ghosts' price. Saronos refused to detail what exactly the Warp Ghosts wanted, but though Daravek offered them ships, slaves and many of the things he possessed, it was Abaddon who won the deal; he simply told Saronos the Warp Ghosts could take what they needed from him. An enraged Daravek threatened Saronos, but returned to his fleet as the Warp Ghost left with Abaddon's group to the Black Legion's flagship the [[Vengeful Spirit]].{{Fn|1e}} The Death Guard Chaos Lord then watched on as Abaddon's fleet entered the [[Warp]] and escaped from the Eye of Terror.{{Fn|1f}}

Despite this setback, Daravek still had a psychic connection with the Black Legion Sorcerer Khayon and he used this to guide Legion Host's fleet out of the Eye of Terror as well. When they neared the [[Cadian Gate]], they found Abaddon's fleet engaged in battle with the [[Black Templars]] [[Chapter]] and quickly fell upon the Black Legion's ships. Now trapped between two foes, Khayon, who was acting in Abaddon's stead aboard the Vengeful Spirit, ordered the Black Legion's fleet to break through the Black Templars blockade and escape into the Warp. Khayon then ordered the Vengeful Spirit to attack Daravek's fleet, in an attempt to goad the Chaos Lord into invading the Black Legion's flagship.{{Fn|1g}} Daravek did not hesitate to do so and led a massive boarding attack on the Vengeful Spirit and personally killed many of its defenders. Before he could reach its bridge however, he was confronted by Khayon and the two fought each other - though this time his attempt to psychically dominate the Sorcerer failed. Khayon had prepared himself for their encounter and had finally realized how Daravek had been able to dominate him. It was not Khayon's soul that Daravek had bound to him, but Khayon's past Daemon familiar [[Gyre]] which had previously been destroyed in battle with a [[clone]] of the [[Primarch]] [[Horus]]. After Gyre had been sent back into the Warp, Daravek had secretly summoned it and bound it to him, which forced the Daemon to turn upon Khayon, though it still had a psychic connection to the Black Legion Sorcerer. It was this connection that had allowed Daravek to have a hold on Khayon, but with Gyre drawn out from the Chaos Lord, that advantage was at an end. Without his hold on the Sorcerer, Daravek was easily overwhelmed by Khayon and was then decapitated by the Sorcerer.{{Fn|1h}} After his death, Daravek's body was crucified above the Vengeful Spirit's oculus{{Fn|1i}} and his Warband soon stopped their attack on the Black Legion's fleet and separated into groups that fled into the Warp. These groups then preyed upon the unsuspecting [[Imperium]] worlds of [[Segmentum Obscurus]]{{Fn|1h}}, though some would eventually join their former enemies and become a part of the Black Legion.{{Fn|1i}}

Tharador Yheng.wikitext:
{{WordBearersPortal}}
'''Tharador Yheng''' was the leader of the [[Cult of the Blade Unsheathed]] who served the [[Word Bearers]] during the [[Battle of Gathalamor]].{{Fn|1a}} Since then she has become a powerful [[Chaos Sorcerer|chaos sorceress]]{{Fn|3a}} and the current master of the [[Hand of Abaddon]].{{Fn|3f}}

==History==
A mortal woman born on [[Gathalamor]], Yheng was charged with [[Dark Apostle]] [[Kar-Gatharr]] with aquiring the artifact known as the Ring of [[Bucharis]] in order to power a Chaos superweapon.{{Fn|1a}} Yheng's cultists were successful in acquiring the ring, and thereafter Kar-Gatharr gave her over to the control of [[Black Legion]] [[Sorcerer]] [[Tenebrus]] in order to steal the artifact back from him should he attempt to flee. Sure enough at the end of the battle Tenebrus attempted to leave Gathalamor with the ring, but after the death of Kar-Gatharr chose to leave with the Sorcerer-Lord{{Fn|1b}}.

Sometime later, Yhend was acting as Tenebrus' acolyte and aided him in his schemes with the [[Word Bearer]]s and the summoning of [[Kairos Fateweaver]] in order to track down the [[Star Child]].{{Fn|2}} She was seen with the rest of the [[Hand of Abaddon]] aboard a [[Blackstone Fortress]] as they gathered together the eight shards of the [[Anathame]].{{Fn|3b}}

Yheng quickly was swept up in the scheming of rival members of the Hand, such as the [[Iron Magus]] who desired the Anathame for herself. Evading death and capture by the Magus' mechanical constructs aboard the Blackstone Fortress, Yheng with the aid of [[Augury]] is able to increase her psychic abilities and experience a vision of the [[Chaos Gods|Dark Gods]] thanks to the empowering properties of the Fortress' [[Noctilith]].{{Fn|3c}} However Yheng is eventually captured by the Magus and brought to the Blackstone Fortress' energy core, but before she can be killed by the [[Dark Mechanicum]] [[Tech-Priest]] the Chaos station is attacked by Imperial forces under the [[Rogue Trader]] [[Katla Helvintr]]. The Blackstone Fortress opens fire at the incoming Imperials, distracting the Iron Magus enough for Yheng to kill her.{{Fn|3d}}

Escaping, Yheng is then confronted by Tenebrus and the two began a heated exchange. Tenebrus demands Yheng come with him but the Fortress itself turns on the Sorcerer, impaling him with spikes that protrude from the wall.{{Fn|3d}} During the subsequent [[Battle of the Stygius Gilt]] Yheng and Augury destroy the Blackstone Fortress' core to deny it to Imperial forces.{{Fn|3d}} Later, the two are able to acquire the reforged [[Anathame]], now dubbed the Culler, by sacrificing the [[Red Corsair]] [[Graeyl Herek]]. Yheng is declared by Augury to be the new master of the Hand of Abaddon and offered [[Daemon Prince|apotheosis]].{{Fn|3f}}

The Arch Zealot of the Redemption.wikitext:
{{NecromundaPortal}}
Based in [[Hive Primus]] on the planet of [[Necromunda (planet)|Necromunda]], the '''Arch Zealot of the Redemption''' is one of the most well-known and feared of all the Redemptor Priests in the Underhive. 

==History==
[[File:RedeemerPic.jpg|thumb|right|Arch Zealot of the Redemption]]
A hermit, he wanders alone through the badlands and the settlements of the Hive, preaching to [[Redemptionist]]s who view him as a mystic and a prophet. He is able to whip them into a furor with just a few words, inciting lynch-mobs, massacres and even campaigns of genocide.{{Fn|1a}}

His views (which include a hatred of just about everybody and his "doctrine of cleansing flame"), have led to him being considered rather extreme by his counterparts within the [[Cult of Redemption]], and to a bounty of 325 credits being placed on his head; some have even called for his banishment from the Crusade. He invariably denounces these opponents as weak-willed traitors to the Redemption, lynching those who don't quickly recant after arguing against him with frenzied mobs he works up into a foaming blood lust with a rabble rousing speech: such is his following among ordinary Redemptionists.{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|2a}}

==Crusade==
After whipping up the crowd with apocalyptic speeches he more often than not leads the mob into battle and has even been known to take money for leading Redemptionist crusades and gangs of [[House Cawdor]] – the House of the Redemption – in gang warfare. Armed with a massive sword (he is an accomplished swordsman), an extremely well-maintained [[flamer]] (he carries a huge canister of fuel on his back to stop it ever running out), [[stub gun]] and wearing [[mesh armour]] under his robes, he also carries his holy book into battle and a banner with the legend "Purge with fire". Those who fight with him never give up, drawing a great strength from his forceful presence and preaching and only stop fighting when the Arch Zealot tells them to or there are no more to kill.{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|1b}}{{Fn|2b}}{{Fn|2c}}

The Herald of Fate.wikitext:
{{ThousandSonsPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a [[Thousand Sons]] [[Sorcerer]] [[Chaos Lord|Lord]] whose forces invaded the [[Imperium|Imperium's]] [[Vidar Sector]] and brought his prophesied message of the Sector's doom to its population.  During the invasion, he led his forces in a conquest of the [[Darkfall System]], but this caused the Sorcerer Lord to transcend to [[Daemon Prince|Daemonhood]] and ended his threat to the Vidar Sector.  Though The Herald's prophesy of doom for the Sector did not come to pass, he had devastated the Darkfall System and left its remaining population scattered and lost - among them, the ruling [[Calcearious Family]] who later fled to the Imperium world of [[Praedis Zeta]].  Hundreds of years later, however, events have unfolded that yet might prove The Herald was correct; the Calcearious Family has been revealed to have degenerated into [[Genestealer]]-worshiping slaves, whose very existence threatens to bring the great swarms of the [[Tyranid]]s to the Sector.{{Fn|1}}

The Newborn.wikitext:
{{QuoteBox
|quote = '''''The destiny of The Lost Child cleaves into the future like a fiery speartip. His destiny is woven into the tapestry of a [[Ardaric Vaanes|great hero]]'s death, the fall of [[Indomitable|a star]], and the rise of [[M'kar|an evil]] thought long dead.'''''
|source=–''A [[Red Corsairs]] [[psyker]], to The Newborn, on [[New Badab]].{{Fn|2}}
|}}
{{IronWarriorsPortal}}
'''The Newborn''' was a mutated clone of [[Uriel Ventris]], loyal to the [[Iron Warriors]] [[Warsmith]] [[Honsou]].

==History==
[[File:Newborn.jpg|thumb|250px|right|The Newborn{{Fn|3}}]]
The Newborn was originally '''Samuquan''', a cadet at [[Scelus]] [[Schola Progenium|Progenium]]. His Schola was raided by the Iron Warriors, and he and several other cadets were kidnapped and taken back to [[Medrengard]] inside the [[Eye of Terror]], to serve as slaves in the Warriors' fortress of [[Khalan-Ghol]]{{Fn|4b}}{{Fn|4f}}{{Fn|4g}}{{Fn|4k}}. Samuquan was later fed to the [[Daemonculaba]], a creation that combined children's bodies with the stolen [[gene-seed]] of captured [[Space Marine]]s.{{Fn|4f}}{{Fn|4g}} Samuquan was combined with the gene-seed of [[Uriel Ventris]], who had been briefly imprisoned inside the Daemonculaba. {{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|1x}}{{Fn|4f}}{{Fn|4g}}

The Newborn became part of Honsou's retinue, replacing the [[Possessed Chaos Space Marine]] [[Onyx (Iron Warriors)|Onyx]] as the Warsmith's bodyguard. He was combat-trained by [[Ardaric Vaanes]], a renegade [[Raven Guard]] who also joined Honsou's retinue.{{Fn|4c}}

He participated in the Skull Harvest{{Fn|2}}.

The Newborn was instrumental in Honsou's [[Invasion of Ultramar]]. Since he carried all of Ventris' memories, he had knowledge of the [[Ultramarines]]' command protocols that allowed Honsou's army, the [[Bloodborn]], to bypass and overwhelm the orbital defenses of [[Tarentus]], [[Talassar]], and [[Calth]].{{Fn|4d}}{{Fn|4f}} He took part in the storming of Calth{{Fn|4e}}, helped Vaanes infiltrate and open [[Guilliman's Gate]]{{Fn|4h}}, and accompanied Honsou to the secret tomb of [[Remus Ventanus|Captain Ventanus]] on Calth{{Fn|4k}}. Uriel and several other Ultramarines tracked Honsou there, and Uriel, with [[Pasanius Lysane]], killed the Newborn.{{Fn|4k}}

==Personality==
Before his death, the Newborn was in constant torment. Honsou had trained him to hate Ventris and the Ultramarines as much as Honsou did, but memories of his past life surfaced at random moments, while the memories he had inherited from Uriel gave him a trace of the Ultramarine's bravery and nobility.{{Fn|4a}}{{Fn|4c}}{{Fn|4j}} The Newborn was painfully aware that he was an abomination: his old life was over, his new life was a pale imitation of someone else's, and the conflict between the two drove him nearly insane.{{Fn|4i}} He blamed Uriel for his tormented existence, but his dying words were to thank Uriel and Pasanius for ending his pain.{{Fn|4k}}

Theodora von Valancius.wikitext:
{{ImperiumPortal}}
'''Theodora von Valancius''' was a [[Rogue Trader]] and the head of [[House von Valancius]], which commands a trade empire in the [[Koronus Expanse]].{{Fn|1a}} She was succeeded by her [[von Valancius heir|heir]].{{Fn|3}}
==History==
[[Image:Rogue Trader Theodora von Valancius Portrait.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Theodora von Valancius Portrait{{Fn|1b}}]]
She maintains the empire with the aid of her [[Rogue Trader House|House]]'s [[Rogue Trader Seneschal|Seneschal]] [[Abelard Werserian]], who has held the position for decades. He is Valancius' loyal right hand and they first met during a joint operation between [[Imperial Navy]] and [[Rogue Trader]] forces. At that time, Valancius was an eccentric, wayward Rogue Trader, while Werserian was a diligent and imperious first officer on an [[Cruiser#Imperial_Navy|Imperial Navy Cruiser]]. Despite being as different as night and day, they learned to appreciate and respect each other and when the operation was done, Valancius claimed Werserian as [[House von Valancius]]' new Seneschal.{{Fn|1a}}

Theodore Viablo.wikitext:
{{ImperiumPortal}}
{{Spoiler|source=The Iron Kingdom (Novel)}}
'''Theodore Viablo'''{{Fn|3}} is a founding member of the [[Logos Historica Verita]], alongside [[Solana (Historitor)|Solana]], [[Deven Mudire]] and [[Fabian Guelphrain]].{{Fn|1a}}

==History==
Viablo was a solemn man, originating from a low gravity world. Shortly before the beginning of the [[Indomitus Crusade]], [[Lord Commander]] [[Guilliman]] would select him to join the newly created [[Logos Historica Verita]]. He would then join [[Fleet Primus]] as it prepared to leave [[Terra]]. There, he joined the other three founding historitors, [[Solana (Historitor)|Solana]], [[Deven Mudire]] and [[Fabian Guelphrain]]. The four would be given tasks to ascertain their talent and compile historical facts in order to establish a true history of the [[Imperium]]. If found to be of sufficient quality, their works would be given to Roboute Guilliman's [[Fleetmaster]]s to read{{Fn|1b}}. Viablo's work would be accepted and he would become a member of the '[[Founding Four]]'{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|3a}}.

The four would then serve beside each other for several years in the Indomitus Crusade's Fleet Primus, training many new recruits for the [[Logos Historica Verita]]. After witnessing the [[Founding]] ceremony of the [[Void Sabres]], the 104th [[Ultima Founding]] they had witnessed together, the founding members were to finally be separated. On the orders of [[Roboute Guilliman]], they were given new duties that sent them away from Fleet Primus - all save for Viablo who was to remain. Lord Guilliman had decided to make the historitor his personal chronicler, much to the envy of Viablo's fellow founding member [[Fabian Guelphrain]]. Guelphrain would eventually acknowledge to himself that Viablo was more suited to the task, due to being more even-tempered, and more diligent, than he was. It would then be several years before the four founding members would be reunited again{{Fn|2}}.

Viablo was ultimately killed during the funeral procession of princess [[Jessivayne Y'Kamidar]] when [[High Queen|High Queen]] [[Orlah Y'Kamidar]] of the [[Ironhold Protectorate]] revolted against the Imperium and Fleet Primus.{{Fn|3b}}

Thess Rahn-Bo.wikitext:
{{AdeptusMechanicusPortal}}
'''Thess Rahn-Bo''' is the cheif datamancer{{Fn|1d}} and cogitatrix{{Fn|1f}} aboard the [[Explorator]] ship ''[[Peregrinus]]''. She is a loyal servant and companion{{Fn|1c}} of the ship's Ductrix and Explorator Superior [[Talin Sherax]], both tech priests are from [[Gryphonne IV]] and witnessed it's destruction.

Rahn-Bo had dedicated her considerable augmentation to further her ability to observe, retain, and analyse, but not to fight. Her sole concession to physical protection was a laspistol holstered at her hip.{{Fn|1c}}

==History==
Rahn-Bo was began her career aboard the explorator ship ''Peregrinus'' as a logi minoris. On her first day in the role, she was issued a laspistol, one of billions stamped from the lost forges of Gryphonne IV. Both a momento and one of her few means to defend herself, she keeps it holstered to her hip to this day.{{Fn|1c}} Eventually, Rahn-bo ascended to the role of cheif datamancer of the ''Peregrinus''.{{Fn|1d}} Thess is Talin's oldest colleague, and addressed each-other familiarly during their concurrent service as initiates. They had known each other for almost two centuries by the time of their departure for [[Ikaneos]].{{Fn|1d}}

{{EmperorsChildrenPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a member of his [[Primarch]] [[Fulgrim]]'s [[Phoenix Guard]] who was honoured with carrying the [[Legion]]'s [[Space Marine Standards|banner]] into battle. He took part in the [[Cleansing of Laeran]], but was killed when his body was set aflame by the [[Laer]]'s weaponry as the Emperor's Children stormed the [[Xenos]]'s final stronghold. To the Legion's shock, the banner slipped from Thestis's dead hands and began to fall to the ground - before it was suddenly grabbed by Fulgrim. The Primarch was horrified to see however, that the fire that had claimed Thestis's life, also quickly consumed the banner before his eyes; leaving only its pole in his hand. Though he was enraged at the banner's loss, Fulgrim noticed that the eagle atop the banner pole remained miraculously untouched by the fire and used it to rally his Legion to redoubled their efforts in destroying the Laer.{{Fn|1}}

When the [[Space Marine Captain]] [[Messinius]] later told them to take their roles as historitors seriously, Mudire was quick to say they would. Thorild.wikitext:
{{SpaceWolvesPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a [[Rune Priest]] in the [[Space Wolves]] [[Chapter]], when the [[Ork]] forces of [[The Beast]] invaded the [[Imperium]] and was part of the [[Wolf Lord]] [[Asger Warfist]]'s [[Great Company]]. 

Once [[Ullanor]], was determined to be where The Beast's forces originated from, Thorild joined as part of the strike force sent to invade the world, in order to kill the Warboss. However, when the strike force arrived at Ullanor they were unable to use their ships to discover the Warboss' location, due to the world being enveloped in [[psychic]] energy. With time running short, [[Chapter Master]] [[Koorland]], asked for the [[Space Marine]] [[Chapter]]s present to gather their Librarians together; in order for them to combine their powers, so they could pierce Ullanor's physic veil. The [[Ultramarines]]' [[Chief Librarian]] [[Vaniel]] was charged with focusing the Librarians' power for the ritual and they entered into a connected trance, where they were able to discover that The Beast was present in an Ork city known as '''Gorkogrod'''. However disaster struck before they were able to learn the exact location of the city, when the Chief Librarian was overwhelmed by the Orks' physic energy. As Vaniel served as a conduit for the ritual, the Ork's energy soon spread to the rest of the Librarians present and nearly overwhelmed all of them. Only Thorild was able to initially resist the Ork's physic power and he was able to help most of the others resist as well before he broke the trance they were in. As soon as he did so though, Vaniel and two other Librarians, who had fallen under the Ork's power, began attacking those around them. The maddened Chief Librarian was able to kill the Librarians [[Redolphio]] and [[Carrigan Nos]] before he was killed by Thorild; which severed the ritual's connection to the Ork's physic energy and ended its influence on the Librarians.{{Fn|1a}}

Though the Librarians were unable to locate Gorkogrod's location, when Koorland presented the information they gathered to the [[Primarch]] [[Vulkan]], he was able to determine where the Ork city was located; after he compared it with the navigational data of Ullanor's surface, that the [[Adeptus Mechanicus]] had gathered{{Fn|1b}}. Soon afterwards the invasion of Gorkogrod began and Thorild and his fellow Liberians were of great aid to the strike force, when they began searching out and fighting against The Beast's numerous [[Weirdboy]]s{{Fn|1c}}. Later when the Warboss' personal [[Gargant]] was discovered, the Rune Priest joined the [[Space Marine]] force that invaded it and they fought their way through to reach The Beast's chambers. When they entered the chambers though, they saw nothing, but a giant statue of The Beast - or so they thought. In reality it was The Beast himself and he began giving off such powerful and deadly waves of physic energy, that it immediately caused Thorild and all of the Librarians present before the Warboss, to burst into flames.{{Fn|1d}}

'''Tibernus''' was an [[Imperial Fist]], who took part in the [[Horus Heresy]]'s [[Siege of Terra]].{{Fn|1}} 
==History==
He was later among the [[Imperial Fists]]{{Fn|1}} that the [[Loyalist Legion|Legion]]'s [[Primarch]], [[Rogal Dorn]], commanded as part of the [[Emperor]]'s [[Teleportation]] boarding attack upon the [[Sons of Horus]]' flagship, the [[Vengeful Spirit]].{{Fn|2a}} They were tasked with killing the [[Traitor|traitorous]] Primarch [[Horus]], in order to save [[Terra]] and the [[Imperium]], but due to Horus' machinations, the Emperor's boarding party was separated from each other.{{Fn|2b}} Worse still for the Imperial Fists aboard the Vengeful Spirit, Dorn had also been torn away from them{{Fn|2c}} and so the [[Huscarls (Imperial Fists)|Huscarl]] [[Diamantis]] took command of the Legion's forces. However the Imperial Forces would all be killed, after they were swarmed by Horus' forces and their remains were later found by a grief stricken Rogal Dorn, who swore to avenge their deaths.{{Fn|1}}

Tirian.wikitext:
{{UltramarinesPortal}}
'''Tirian''' is a [[Space Marine Sergeant]] from the [[Ultramarines]] [[2nd Company (Ultramarines)|2nd Company]], under [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Cato Sicarius]].  He commands one of the two [[Devastator Squad]]s assigned to the 2nd Company.  His squad, nicknamed "[[Guilliman]]'s Hammer" is renowned for their steadiness and unwavering conduct in the heat of battle.{{Fn|1a}}

==History==
===Black Reach===
During the [[Assault on Black Reach]] in 855 [[M41]]{{Fn|1b}}, Squad Tirian were deployed to [[Black Reach]] with the rest of the Second Company against [[Waaagh!]] [[Zanzag]]. After the liberation of Ghospora Hive from the [[Ork]]s, Sicarius assigned Tirian, plus [[Tactical Squad]]s [[Praxor Manorian|Manorian]] and [[Iulus Fennion|Fennion]], to garrison the hive in case of an Ork counterattack, while the remainder of the Company was tasked to hunt down the [[Warboss]].{{Fn|2}}

===Espandor===
During the [[Invasion of Ultramar]] by the [[Bloodborn]], in 854999.M41{{Fn|1b}}, the 2nd Company was deployed to [[Espandor]].{{Fn|3}}

Titus Cassar.wikitext:
{{CollegiaTitanicaPortal}}
{{ImperiumPortal}}
'''Titus Cassar''' was a [[Moderati|Moderati Primus]] of the [[Legio Mortis]] [[Imperator Battle Titan]] ''[[Dies Irae]]'' during the [[Horus Heresy]].{{fn|1a}}

==Biography==
Secretly, Cassar was a member of the [[Lectitio Divinitatus]], a cult that worshipped the [[Emperor of Mankind]] as a divine being.{{fn|1b}} He was often ridiculed for this belief by his friend and fellow moderati [[Jonah Aruken]], although the latter came to him for spiritual comfort after the Titan faced an army of [[Plague Zombie|walking corpses]] on [[Davin]]'s moon and Horus Lupercal was wounded by the [[Anathame]].{{fn|1c}} He subsequently attracted a following of fellow worshipers, who gathered in the nooks and crannies of the ''[[Vengeful Spirit]]''{{fn|1d}}, and was one of the first to refer to [[Euphrati Keeler]] as "the saint", after she banished a [[Daemon]] from the ship's library{{fn|1e}}.

[[Kyril Sindermann]] turned to Cassar when Keeler was in danger{{fn|2a}}, and he dragged Aruken along against the mute assassin [[Maggard]].{{fn|2b}} The experience made his faith all the stronger, which Aruken resented as it would endanger their team and his own ambition.{{fn|2c}} During the [[Battle of Isstvan III]], after the virus strike and firestorm, [[Esau Turnet|Princeps Turnet]] ordered the moderatii to open fire on the [[Death Guard]] loyalists, and Cassar confronted Turnet in a brief autopistol duel. However, as Cassar intended to kill Turnet for his betrayal of the God-Emperor, Aruken — determined to gain command of his own Titan one day — killed his friend and ended the duel.{{fn|2d}}

'''Titus Prayto''' was the [[Ultramarines]] [[Loyalist Legion|Legion]]'s [[Chief Librarian]], during [[The Scouring]].{{Fn|2}} 
===Biography===
He initially served in the [[Great Crusade]] as a [[Librarian]], but after the [[Edict of Nikaea]] Prayto had to resign from the [[Ultramarines]]' [[Librarius (Fortress-monastery)|Librarius]] and assumed normal duties as a [[Centurion (Rank)|Centurion]]. However due to the [[Word Bearers]]' treachery in the [[Horus Heresy]]'s [[Battle of Calth]], the Ultramarines' [[Primarch]], [[Roboute Guilliman]], reversed the Edict for his Legion and Prayto became a Librarian once more.{{Fn|1a}}

As the [[Horus Heresy]] continued, Prayto became a close adviser to [[Guilliman]] and he was used to try and examine the [[Primarch]] [[Lion El'Jonson]]'s true motives, when the [[Dark Angels]] visited [[Macragge]]. During that time, Prayto was badly injured by the [[Night Lords]]' Primarch [[Konrad Curze]], as the [[Traitor Legion]] went on a rampage across [[Imperium Secundus]]' [[Capital World]].{{Fn|1b}}

Prayto went on to survive the [[Horus Heresy]] and was the [[Ultramarines]]' [[Chief Librarian]], during [[The Scouring]].{{Fn|2}}

Tjejren.wikitext:
{{InquisitionPortal}}
'''Tjejren''' is a [[Radical]] [[Inquisitor]], who turned his [[Interrogator]] [[Remo]] into a [[Daemonhost]].{{Fn|1}} 
==History==
His [[Radicalism]] led him to be hunted in the eastern part of the [[Realm of Ultramar]], during the [[Plague Wars]], by the forces of [[Tetrarch of Ultramar|Tetrarch]] [[Felix (Tetrarch)|Felix]]. The [[Inquisitor]] and his retinue, however, inflicted heavy losses on their attackers, which allowed Tjejren to escape. [[Remo]] was captured, though, and Tetrarch Felix planned to destroy the [[Daemonhost]] [[Interrogator]] immediately. [[Lord Commander]] [[Guilliman]] interceded, however, as truly believed Remo's Daemon could tell him what was occurring on the corrupted [[Ultramar]] world [[Iax]]. It was Guilliman's hope that the answers Remo's Daemon provided him, would allow him to prevent Iax from being forever lost to the [[Imperium]]. In order to ensure his questions would be answered, Guilliman had Remo secretly taken from Felix's hold and transferred to his flagship [[Macragge's Honour]]. A furious Felix would soon confront him, and attempted to stop Guilliman from making a horrible mistake. In the Tetrach's eyes, Remo was now a creature of both [[Tjejren]] and [[Chaos]] and warned Guilliman that nothing the Interrogator's Daemon said could be trusted. Guilliman claimed that Tjejren still believed he still loyally serves the Imperium and may one day actually do so again. The Lord Commander claimed the same was true for Remo, as the Interrogator's soul still clung to his body. This in turn, the Lord Commander thought, would force the Interrogator's Daemon to truthfully answer his questions.{{Fn|1}}

Tobris Ekharth.wikitext:
{{ImperiumPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was the [[Master of the Administratum]] and a powerful member of the [[High Lords of Terra]] in mid-[[M32]] during the [[War of the Beast]]. Blind in one eye which bore a long scar across his face, Ekharth was close to the powerful [[Lord High Admiral]] [[Lansung]] and one of the key members of his alliance that ensured his dominance on the Senatorum.{{Fn|1}} During the war against [[The Beast]], the ''de facto'' ruling triumvirate of Lansung, Ekharth, and [[Udin Macht Udo]] ensured Imperial inaction and internal squabbling.{{Fn|2}}

Following Lansung's fall from grace after the appearance of an Ork [[Attack Moon]] over [[Terra]], Ekharth abandoned his former ally and instead pledged his support to [[Juskina Tull]] and her disastrous [[Proletarian Crusade]].{{Fn|3}} Ekharth again abandoned his ally, this time [[Lord Commander]] [[Udin Macht Udo]], when he was overthrown by [[Imperial Fists]] [[Chapter Master]] [[Koorland]] and the [[Inquisition]].{{Fn|4}}

Later, Ekharth was seen conversing with [[Drakan Vangorich]], pleading with the [[Grand Master of Assassins]] to do something about Koorland and the Space Marines usurping of power from the High Lords. Vangorich regarded him with disgust.{{Fn|5}} When [[Vulkan]] returned to lead the Imperium against The Beast, Ekharth was horrified when the Primarch broke administrative protocol and utilized Administratum resources without his own approval. Despite his timid protests, his protests were ignored by Vulkan and Koorland.{{Fn|6}} Ekharth again led opposition to Koorland alongside [[Mesring]], this time forbidding the creation of the [[Deathwatch]]. However when the Ork [[Attack Moon]] over Terra reactivated, Ekharth realized he was defeated and backed down.{{Fn|7}}

After the war, Ekharth was opposed by the attempts of Vangorich and [[Inquisitorial Representative]] [[Wienand]] in naming [[Imperial Fists]] [[Chapter Master]] [[Maximus Thane]] as the new Lord Commander of the Imperium. However he was again overruled and backed down. Subsequently, Ekharth was among the High Lords killed by Vangorich in [[The Beheading]]. How he died is unknown, but he was replaced with an impostor that likely was a [[Callidus Assassin]]. This impostor later murdered Ekharth's allies, Lord Commander Militant [[Verreault]] and Lord High Admiral [[Lansung]] and went on to serve as the Master of the Administratum in Vangorich's puppet cabinet.{{Fn|8}}

Tolbek.wikitext:
{{ThousandSonsPortal}}
[[Image:Tolbek.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Tolbek during the Horus Heresy]]
'''Tolbek''' was a former member of the [[Thousand Sons]] [[legion]]. He was an Adept of the [[Pyrae]] Cult during the [[Great Crusade]], and, after the Legion's escape to the [[Planet of the Sorcerers]], one of the first members to join the [[Cabal of Ahriman|cabal]] formed by [[Ahzek Ahriman]] to cast the [[Rubric of Ahriman]].{{Fn|1c}} Tolbek was part of Ahriman's fellowship to reclaim the [[Shards of Magnus]] during the Heresy.{{Fn|2}}

After the Rubric's failure, the entire [[Cabal of Ahriman|Cabal]], including Tolbek and Ahriman, were exiled from the Legion.{{Fn|1a}} After his exile, Tolbek joined [[Amon]]'s warband, [[The Brotherhood of Dust]].{{Fn|1}}

The next time Tolbek met [[Ahriman]] again was thousands of years after their exile, aboard the captured ship ''[[Titan Child]]''.{{Fn|1a}} The Brotherhood of Dust was searching for Ahriman, and Tolbek unknowingly encountered his former brother, traveling incognito with the warband [[The Harrowing]], that had captured the ''Titan Child''. Tolbek asked Ahriman to leave with him, and, when Ahriman refused, attacked him with a psychic blow. Ahriman deflected it and killed Tolbek and the Harrowing's leadership, leaving only a sorcerer named [[Maroth]], Tolbek's two [[Rubricae]] bodyguards and himself as the only survivors in the room.{{Fn|1c}}
In Ritual of the Damned, Tolbek somehow returns to Prospero. It's not explained if he was revived or brought back through time-bending sorcery.{{Fn|3}}

Tolmach.wikitext:
'''Tolmach''' was a [[Emperor's Spears#Organisation|Druid]] [[Chaplain]] of the [[Emperor's Spears]]' 3rd Warhost.

==Biography==
Hailing from [[Nemeton]]'s Novontei Tribe, unlike many of the Spears who initially shunned the [[Mentor Legion]] liaison [[Amadeus]], Tolmach immediately displayed professional and polite attitudes towards the Astartes.{{Fn|1a}} When the [[Exilarchy]] boarded the Spears flagship ''[[Hex]]'', Tolmach was the first to die against a child [[Rogue Psyker]].{{Fn|1b}}

After his death, some of Tolmach's organs (alongside those of [[Faelan]]) were used in the Calgarisian Rites performed on Amadeus that both saved the [[Mentors|Mentor]] and allowed him to cross the [[Rubicon Primaris]]. A statue was made in his honour on the barrow deck of the ''Hex''; its plaque mentioned that Tolmach had once he once headbutted a [[planetary governor]] in front of an entire royal court, and expressed a feeling of loss at his death at the hands of the [[The Pure|Pure]].{{Fn|1c}}

Tomas Beije.wikitext:
{{QuoteBox |quote = '''''"How truly it has been said that the glory we gain blinds us first with its lustre."'''
- Tomas Beije, quoting from Caddaway's "Paths to Damnation".'''''{{Fn|1d}} |}} {{AstraMilitarumPortal}} '''Tomas Beije''' was [[regiment]]al [[Commissar]] of the [[Tallarn 229th]] during its deployment to [[Adumbria]] in [[937.M41]].{{Fn|1c}} ==History== {{spoiler|source=The Traitor's Hand (Novel)}} Beije was in the same [[Schola Progenium]] class as [[Ciaphas Cain]], and the two disliked each other intensely. Beije was always correct in adherence to rules and his piety to the [[Emperor]], and was quick to report any of his fellow cadets who he felt were not{{Fn|1a}}. Cain and several of his less reverent classmates often delighted in playing pranks on their more strait-laced comrades, especially Beije{{Fn|1b}}. The two did not cross paths again until almost twenty years later, when the Tallarn 229th was deployed to [[Adumbria]] alongside the [[Valhallan 597th]], Cain's regiment. Like many [[Tallarn]] regiments, the 229th was intensely pious, which made Cain feel that Beije's assignment marked a stroke of good judgment (or luck) on the part of the [[Departmento Munitorum]]: in any other regiment, Beije would likely have been "accidentally" shot during his first engagement{{Fn|1a}}. [[Inquisitor]] [[Amberley Vail]], editing Cain's [[Cain Archive|memoirs]], attached several dispatches by Beije to his superiors, which included quotes from [[Redemptionist]] tracts of ''"dubious theology and even worse literacy."''{{Fn|1c}}{{Fn|1d}} By the time of their next meeting, Cain had become a celebrated Hero of the Imperium, and a personal friend of [[Lord General]] [[Zyvan]]. These facts filled Beije with a combination of bafflement, moral outrage, and seething envy. To his mind, it was somehow wrong - not to say impossible - that a man as lacking in discipline and proper fear of the Emperor as Cain should have risen so high, while Beije himself had not{{Fn|1b}}. Beije also shared his Tallarn comrades' low regard for [[Imperial Guard Regiment]]s that included women, which increased the friction between the Tallarns and the Valhallans prior to their deployment{{Fn|1a}}{{Fn|1b}}. During the Adumbria campaign, to defend the world from a [[Chaos]] invasion, Beije sought to undermine Cain at several times. In one of the above-mentioned dispatches to the Lord General's office, he implied that there was something at best cowardly, and at worst sinister, in the fact that Cain had been attached to two separate Guard contingents that had stumbled onto the sites of cultist summoning rituals, and, in both cases, had not arrived until after these rituals were completed{{Fn|1d}}. Later, he asked an assembly of the Guard headquarters whether it was really believable that Cain had defeated a [[World Eater]] [[Chaos Space Marine]] in single combat. Cain played down his role in the encounter, as usual, and managed to convince nearly everyone assembled{{Fn|1e}}. During the climactic battle of the campaign, Cain commandeered a [[Imperial Transport|drop ship]] which had been ordered to the frontlines, and diverted it to an oceanic dredger, where [[Slaanesh]]i [[cultist]]s were conducting a summoning ritual. Beije seized on this action and pursued the dropship with a squad of Tallarn troopers, declaring Cain under arrest for desertion, cowardice and subverting military resources{{Fn|1f}}. When the Valhallan troopers protested, Beije brazenly ordered his Tallarn escorts to shoot them all down. Fortunately, the Tallarns were sensible enough to recognize that they were grossly outnumbered, and held back{{Fn|1g}}. While deriding Cain's claimed reasons for diverting the troopship, Beije also made the mistake of insulting the 597th's commander, [[Colonel]] [[Regina Kasteen]]. Cain stiffly challenged him to a duel when the combat was over{{Fn|1g}}. Cain broke the standoff by declaring that their mission was in deadly earnest - a fact reinforced when battle erupted between the cultists and an arriving force of World Eaters. Beije, confused, could only order his troopers to follow after Cain as he and the Valhallans charged ahead in the World Eaters' wake{{Fn|1g}}. Fittingly, Beije was personally present when Cain, for the second time, narrowly defeated a World Eater with his [[chainsword]], a feat which cemented his reputation with the Valhallans and the Tallarns alike{{Fn|1h}}. Likewise, Beije's accusations of cowardice rang hollow when Cain and his troops confronted the [[Daemon]]ess, [[Emeli Duboir]], and banished her back to the [[Warp]]. Beije did not distinguish himself during the action, being noticeably petrified by the appearance of the daemon{{Fn|1i}}. For whatever reason, Beije still insisted on putting Cain before a [[Commissariat]] tribunal. The results were all Cain could have hoped for: the tribunal, with the help of some discreet information provided by Lord General Zyvan, found Cain innocent of any wrongdoing and commended him for his heroic actions; and on its own motion, brought charges against Beije for conduct unbecoming a commissar. The tribunal found that Beije's actions, had he carried them out, could have had the worst consequences for the planet.{{Fn|1j}} Cain, writing his own memoirs years later, harshly echoed this sentiment, reflecting that Beije's ''"pig-headed stupidity... almost ended up handing an Imperial world to the [[Ruinous Powers]] neatly gift-wrapped with a pretty pink bow[.]"''{{Fn|1a}} Beije was stripped of his rank and was almost certainly facing execution, but Cain promised to speak in his defense, and testify that Beije's actions, however ill-advised, came from only the best intentions. Privately, Cain reflected that shooting him would not do anyone much good, and that it would be infinitely more satisfying to have Beije in his debt for the remainder of their lives.{{Fn|1j}} Faced with the prospect of a duel with Cain, Beije offered his humble apologies to Colonel Kasteen, before making a hasty exit.{{Fn|1j}} ==See also== ===Related articles=== *[[List of Commissars]] ==Sources== *1: [[The Traitor's Hand (Novel)]] - [[Ciaphas Cain: Hero of the Imperium (Omnibus)]] **{{Endn|1a}}: Chapter 1, pgs. 501–505 **{{Endn|1b}}: Chapter 2, pgs. 515-518 **{{Endn|1c}}: Editorial Note after Chapter 7, pgs. 588–589 **{{Endn|1d}}: Editorial Note after Chapter 10, pgs. 623–624 **{{Endn|1e}}: Chapter 14, pg. 666 **{{Endn|1f}}: Chapter 17, pgs. 716–717 **{{Endn|1g}}: Chapter 18, pgs. 723–725 **{{Endn|1h}}: Chapter 19, pgs. 736–737 **{{Endn|1i}}: Chapter 20, pgs. 751–752 **{{Endn|1j}}: Chapter 21, pgs. 755–756 {{DEFAULTSORT:Beije, Tomas}} [[Category:Characters (Human)]] [[Category:Characters (Imperial Guard Commissars)]] [[Category:Ciaphas Cain (Novel Series)]]

[[M30]] |Active Period =[[M30]] - 900s.[[M41]] |Death =900s.[[M41]] |Cause of Death =Killed by the [[Heart of Blood]] |Species =[[Human]] |Type =[[Astartes]] |Gender =Male |Relatives =[[Perturabo]]
("Father" via [[gene-seed]]) |Occupation ='' '' *[[Warsmith]] of the [[Iron Warriors]] [[Stor-Bezashk]] |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] (Former) **[[Iron Warriors]] *[[Chaos]] **[[Chaos Undivided]] |Notes = }} '''Toramino''' was one of the great [[Warsmith]]s, commanding a [[Grand Company]] of the [[Iron Warriors]] in life, and serving as the [[castellan]] of an ancient and mighty (but unnamed) fortress on [[Medrengard]]. ===History=== ====Heresy-era==== Prior to the [[Horus Heresy]], Toramino was a [[Warsmith]] of the [[Iron Warriors]] and master of the [[Stor-Bezashk]]. Following the death of [[Erasmus Golg]] in the [[Battle of the Phall System]] and the disgrace of [[Harkor]] in the [[First Siege of Hydra Cordatus]], two of the three positions in the prestigious [[Triarch]] — [[Perturabo]]'s inner council - were open. [[First Captain]] [[Forrix]] nominated [[Barban Falk]] and Toramino, but Perturabo chose to elevate Falk and [[Kroeger]], but not Toramino.{{Fn|3a}} Enraged, Toramino attempted to scheme with Harkor to bring down Kroeger. Toramino however was unsuccessful, and he faced a backlash for incidents of friendly fire during [[Battle of Iydris|the fighting]] on [[Iydris]].{{Fn|3b}} ====Post-Heresy==== During the [[13th Black Crusade]], Falk (now known simply as "The Warsmith") [[Siege of Hydra Cordatus|assaulted]] the planet of [[Hydra Cordatus]], seeking to attain the [[Imperial Fist]] [[gene-seed]] that was stored there. Under his command were Captains [[Forrix]], Kroeger, and [[Honsou]]. Eventually, the Warsmith succeeded in conquering the planet. Although Imperial defenders tried to destroy the gene-seed before he could reach it, he moved quickly and reached the cryo-chambers before they could finish. Already favored in the eyes of the [[Gods of Chaos]], the Warsmith was promoted to [[daemonhood]] for such an accomplishment. Just before his ascension, he named Honsou as his successor Warsmith. The remaining Imperials were subsequently all killed or enslaved by Honsou's forces, who then withdrew back into the [[Eye of Terror]] with the intact gene-seed.{{Fn|2}} Upon learning that Honsou had returned to [[Medrengard]] with such a prize, his fellow Warsmiths, [[Berossus]] and Toramino confronted him in his mighty citadel of [[Khalan-Ghol]]. They demanded that he give them their share of the spoils, as previously promised by the Warsmith under whom Honsou served. When Honsou refused, Toramino threatened him with war, which he dared Toramino to incite. Toramino and Berossus both declared war on Honsou and exited Khalan-Ghol.{{Fn|1b}} ====The War==== Toramino and Berossus brought their armies to the gates of Khalan-Ghol, where they proceeded to lay siege to the fortress: constructing trenches, fortifying artillery, and the like. Berossus's armies were far more aggresive than Toramino's, who seemed content to sit back and let his ally bear the brunt of the fighting (which he did).{{Cite This}} Berossus's forces succeeded in breaching the walls of Khalan-Ghol and Berossus himself almost killed Honsou, but Honsou's life-ward, [[Onyx (Iron Warriors)|Onyx]], broke open Berossus's sarcophagus and Honsou tore out his [[Mind Impulse Unit]] and crushed the remains of the [[Dreadnought]]'s skull. Berossus's retinue defected to Honsou, unnerved by Berossus's defeat, and resentful that their overlord, Toramino, was content to sit back from the front lines and let others do the fighting.{{Fn|1c}} The siege devolved into a deadlock for some time until [[Uriel Ventris]] and [[Pasanius Lysane]], two fugitive [[Ultramarines]], unleashed the [[Heart of Blood]], a [[Greater Daemon of Khorne]] imprisoned within Khalan-Ghol. As the daemon broke free, the fortress was destroyed, but the Heart of Blood sensed the hateful presence of [[sorceror]]s among Toramino's army, and the daemon resolved to smash the army apart and dismember its lord. Honsou, having lost the siege but won the war, could only laugh.{{Fn|1d}} During his assault on the [[Indomitable]] space fort, Honsou noted that Toramino was dead, likely having been killed by the Heart of Blood.{{Fn|4}} ===Appearance=== ''"Lord Toramino wore a suit of exquisitely tooled [[power armour]], handcrafted on [[Olympia]] itself and burnished to a mirror sheen. Its trims were edged with arabesques of carven gold and onyx chevrons and its every surface wrought with terrible sigils of ruin. An ochre cloak of woven metallic thread, stronger than adamantium, billowed around his wide frame, partially obscuring the skull-masked symbol of the Iron Warriors on one shoulder guard and his own personal heraldry of a mailed fist above a plan view of a breached redoubt on the other... Long white hair, pulled into a tight scalp-lock, trailed down his back and his stern, patrician features were pinched and angular - speaking of long years of bitter experience. His eyes were opalescent orbs of gold, smouldering with suppressed rage beneath thick brows."''{{Fn|1a}} ===Sources=== {{Cite}} *{{Endn|1}}: [[Dead Sky, Black Sun (Novel)]] — [[The Ultramarines Omnibus]] **{{Endn|1a}}: Prologue, pg. 524 **{{Endn|1b}}: Prologue, pgs. 525–528 **{{Endn|1c}}: Chapter Eighteen, pgs. 715–718 **{{Endn|1d}}: Chapter Twenty-Two, pgs. 760–761 *{{Endn|2}}: [[Storm of Iron (Novel)]],{{cite this}} *3: [[Angel Exterminatus (Novel)]] **{{Endn|3a}}: Chapter Two **{{Endn|3b}}: {{Cite This}} *{{Endn|4}}: [[Iron Warrior (Novella)]], Chapter Four [[Category:Characters (Iron Warriors)]] [[Category:Ultramarines (Novel Series)]]
